statement.p: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve \sqrt{x+3y}+\sqrt{5xy} = 9 at the point (1, 5).
The slope of the tangent line to the curve at the given point is .

solution.p: Differentiating implicitly with respect to x gives \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x+3y}} + \frac{3}{2 \sqrt{x+3y}} \, \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{5}{2 \sqrt{5xy}} \left( y + x \, \frac{dy}{dx} \right) = 0, or (multiplying by 2 \sqrt{5xy} \sqrt{x+3y}) 1 \sqrt{5xy} + 3 \sqrt{5xy} \; \frac{dy}{dx} + 5 y \sqrt{x+3y} + 5 x \sqrt{x+3y} \; \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, so \left( 3 \sqrt{5xy} + 5 x \sqrt{x+3y} \right) \, \frac{dy}{dx} = - \left( 1 \sqrt{5xy} + 5 y \sqrt{x+3y} \right), and therefore \frac{dy}{dx} = - \frac {1 \sqrt{5xy} + 5 y \sqrt{x+3y}}{3 \sqrt{5xy} + 5 x \sqrt{x+3y}}. If x = 1 and y = 5, then \sqrt{x+3y} = 4, \sqrt{5xy} = 5, and hence the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point (1, 5) is \frac{dy}{dx} \Bigg|_{(x, y) = (1, 5)} = - \frac {1 \left( 5 \right) + 5 \left( 5 \right) \left( 4 \right)} {3 \left( 5 \right) + 5 \left( 1 \right) \left( 4 \right)} = -3.
